title: Trade between countries
examples: Why is it good for a country to buy things from another country?
What does it mean when we talk about comparative advantage?
Can a country survive without trading with others?

explain.say: Today we are learning about trade between countries. Say what you think trade means to you.

items: Trade is the exchange of these

explain.say: When a country buys goods from another, we call those imports. For example, if the US buys coffee from Brazil, that is an import.

draw.text: Imports: goods brought into a country

explain.say: When a country sells goods to another, we call those exports. For instance, if Japan sells cars to Canada, those cars are Japanese exports.

draw.text: Exports: goods sent from a country

explain.say: Comparative advantage means doing something best compared to others. It is about opportunity cost.
A real-life example is smartphones. Some countries are very good at making the screens, while others are good at making the chips. They trade these parts.
The most common mistake is thinking every country must be the absolute best at everything. You must focus on what you are relatively best at.

draw.text: Focus on what you do best

faq.q: Why do countries trade with each other?
faq.a: Countries trade to get things they cannot make themselves, or things they can make less efficiently. They trade to improve their standard of living.
asks: What is the main reason for international trade?
Why is trade beneficial for nations?

faq.q: Is it always better to import things?
faq.a: No, it is not always better. A country must balance its imports with its exports to maintain a healthy economy.
asks: Can a country rely only on imports?
What is the balance between buying and selling goods?

faq.q: What is the difference between importing and exporting?
faq.a: Imports are goods coming into your country from another place. Exports are goods leaving your country to go somewhere else.
asks: If I buy coffee from Colombia, is that an import or export?
Which direction does the goods travel for imports?

faq.q: How does comparative advantage help a country decide what to make?
faq.a: It helps them see which goods they can produce at a lower opportunity cost than other countries. This means they have a unique edge.
asks: What is the role of opportunity cost in trade?
How do I find my comparative advantage?

faq.q: Does every country have a comparative advantage in something?
faq.a: Yes, every country has at least one area where it can produce goods relatively well. This is the basis of all trade.
asks: Must every nation have a specialty?
Is it possible for a country to have no advantage?

facts: Imports are goods bought from other countries.
Exports are goods sold to other countries.
Comparative advantage means being best at something relative to others.
Trade allows countries to specialize and exchange goods.

quiz.say: If Country X sells textiles to Country Y, what is this transaction?
quiz.why: The goods are leaving Country X and going to Country Y.

wrong.0: This is a measure of total trade, not the direction of one good.
wrong.1: This is the reason for trade, not the action itself.
wrong.3: This suggests the goods are coming into Country X.

quiz.say: A country that buys oil from Saudi Arabia is engaging in:
quiz.why: The oil is entering the buying country from Saudi Arabia.

wrong.0: This would mean the country was selling oil to Saudi Arabia.
wrong.1: This describes a skill, not the movement of goods.
wrong.2: This refers to the overall amount, not the single transaction.

quiz.say: If Country A can make shoes or wheat, and Country B can make shoes or wheat, but Country A gives up less wheat to make shoes than Country B, Country A has the:
quiz.why: It means Country A sacrifices less of another good to make shoes.

wrong.0: This is the concept being measured, not the advantage itself.
wrong.2: This means being better at everything, which is not what is stated.
wrong.3: This is an economic measure of money, not a production skill.
